en: The Jātaka:
The Collection of Ten Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Four Gates.
4. The Saṅkha Jātaka:
“O Saṅkha, you are one who has heard much and knows the Dhamma;
you have seen both recluses and brahmins.”
"Why do you utter lamentations at an improper time?
Who else indeed could be your respondent but I?
"O beautiful one, beautiful one, with your shell-like neck so well-adorned..."
Taking it in a golden bowl,
he said to me, "Eat this meal," out of his wealth of faith.
“Such a one as this,
O Brahmin, having seen such a Yakkha,
a person desiring to dwell in happiness would question him.”
"Arise and ask him with palms joined:
'Are you a goddess, or are you a human being?'—[that] which you perceive me with ease. "That which you perceive me with ease..."
"You say to me, 'Eat your meal';
I ask you, O lady of great majesty,
are you a goddess or are you a human?"
“O Devī, I am Saṅkhā, possessed of great power,
come here into the midst of the ocean waters;
compassionate toward us and not of a corrupt mind.”
I have come here for your very sake.
Here are food, drink, bedding, and seats,
as well as various kinds of vehicles in great numbers.
“I shall bestow upon you everything,
whatever you have desired in your mind.
“Whatever has been offered and sacrificed by me...”
"You are the sovereign over all of us,
O lady of beautiful limbs; you with lovely hips, beautiful brows, and a slender waist—
of what karma is this the result for me?"
“On a hot road, O Brahmin, he provided a single bhikkhu—
whose feet were blistered, who was thirsty and exhausted—
with conch-shell sandals.”
“May that offering be a cow of plenty for you today.
“Let it be a ship provided with planks, not leaking,
and driven by the wind of *eraka* grass.”
“There is no ground here for another vehicle;
lead me this very day to Moliṇī.
Delighted, joyful, and thrilled, she went there.
Having fashioned a beautifully adorned boat,
he took a conch shell and, together with a man,
brought it to the city of Sādhuramma.
The Saṅkha Jātaka is the fourth.
